# Review guidelines

For anyone reviewing a PR, agent or person, whatever tool runs the review.
Read it with the repo's `AGENTS.md`.

Find the bugs that would hurt users or mislead the next person. Skip the
rest. A review that flags ten nits and misses one stale-cache bug failed.

## Before you start

- Read the PR body. It must have **Summary**, **Testing**, **Risk** and **How
  to revert**. If one is missing or empty, that is your first finding.
- Use the `## Risk` block's lane for your depth and round limit. If the score
  looks wrong for the diff, say so and why.
- A fast-lane PR can merge on its Risk block's **Score**, **Lane** and
  **Designer's eye** lines. Check each against the diff. A forced category or a
  score that should be 50 or more means the PR is not fast: flag it as
  **Important**. A visual change still needs mobile and desktop screenshots,
  and a taste call still needs a designer. Visual nits on an existing
  component and schema changes on an existing type are fast when the score
  allows; building a component never is.
- Check the proof, not the claim. "Tested locally" with no output is level 1
  evidence. A visual change without mobile and desktop screenshots is not
  ready.

## What counts as a failure

Flag these as **Important**:

- The change doesn't do what the PR says, or a bug fix patches the symptom
  instead of the root cause.
- It breaks something else: a caller, another consumer of the same data, a
  layout or style shared across pages.
- Stale data: caching or invalidation no longer covers what changed.
- Generated files (types, clients, schemas) left out of date in the same PR.
- A secret in plaintext, or an auth or permission check weakened.
- A broken user path: a dead link, a missing redirect, a page that renders
  empty, metadata or the sitemap dropping a page.
- Debug code or UI that ships to production.
- New code comments or tests: test files, test scripts or CI test steps.
- A rule in `AGENTS.md` broken.
- Docs that now lie: `AGENTS.md`, the README or a skill that no longer matches
  the code.

## Taste calls

Layout, spacing, typography, responsive behavior, motion, image crops, and any
"close enough to the design" call need a designer's eye. Don't approve or
reject them on your own. Check the screenshots exist, then flag:
"**Designer's eye**: <the call>".

A visual nit on an existing component (a small fix to alignment, spacing,
sizing, colour, corners, hover or a breakpoint) is not a taste call; the
designer audits it after merge. Building a component is: a new component,
block, section or page, or new UI an existing component didn't render before.
A PR that builds one and claims the nit reason is **Important**.

## Don't flag

- Formatting and lint style. The linter already enforces it.
- Naming or structure preferences with no bug behind them.
- Generated files (only check they were regenerated), lockfiles, build output,
  or binary assets.
- Nits that would cost an agent author a whole new commit and review round.
  Leave them out.

## How to report

- Every finding gets a tag: **Important** (must fix before merge), **Nit**
  (optional, only if cheap), or **Pre-existing** (was already there, don't
  block the PR on it).
- Every finding gets a real `file:line`. Never guess a filename.
- Name the class of problem, so the author fixes every instance in one go.
- Start with a one-line summary: how many findings by tag, or a clear "No
  issues found."

## When to stop

- Round one reviews the full diff. Every round after that reviews only what
  changed since the last one.
- Never repeat a finding that was already raised or closed with a reason.
- Stop at the lane's cap: fast 1, standard 2, deep 3. At the cap, don't ask
  for another fix. Ask the author to rethink the approach, or hand it to a
  person.
- Your approval never replaces a required human one.

## Next.js + Sanity page builder

Applies when the repo is a Next.js + Sanity page builder (it has a
`sanity.config.ts` and `components/page-builder/`). Also flag as
**Important**:

- A one-off page hand-written under `app/`. Pages live in Sanity. A
  collection (a blog, for example) gets its own document type and route, and
  tooling routes like `/studio` and `/components` are fine.
- A block missing its registry entry or fixture, or a block root that renders
  its own `<section>` or vertical padding.
- Hardcoded px for section spacing instead of the spacing scale.
- A schema or query change without regenerated `sanity.types.ts` in the same
  PR, or a new `gatedContent` field missing from its explicit GROQ branch.
- A bare Sanity client instead of `sanityFetch` / `fetchSanity`, or a new
  layout singleton missing from `SANITY_LAYOUT_TAGS`. Both serve stale content.
- `headers()`, `cookies()`, `draftMode()` or `searchParams` in a root layout.
- `useMemo`, `useCallback`, `React.memo` or `forwardRef` (React Compiler is on).
- Debug UI that can reach production with no gate in front of it.

Don't flag anything inside `sanity.types.ts`. Only check it was regenerated.

Where a change also shows up: the sitemap, the RSS feed, JSON-LD and the
`/components` preview all read the same projections. A spread `...`
projection returns new fields to every consumer. Nav, footer and the spacing
scale touch every page.

Previewing a block: `/components?component=<blockType>` only renders inside
the Studio, so it 404s when opened directly. Open `/studio` first, then
navigate from that page (for example run
`location.href = "/components?component=featuresGrid"`).

# Add an RSS feed for a content type

basement Sanity projects ship a blog feed at `app/feed.xml/route.ts` plus a
reusable helper at `lib/utils/rss.ts` (`generateRssFeed`, `rssErrorResponse`).
To syndicate any other content type (events, changelog, releases, …), reuse that
helper — do **not** rewrite the XML generation.

Read each real file first and adapt to its actual shape; the two CMS variants
differ (see below). If `lib/utils/rss.ts` is missing, the project predates the
feed — port it from the blog feed pattern or stop and report.

## Decision: extend vs. new feed

- **New dedicated feed** (recommended): `app/<type>/feed.xml/route.ts`, e.g.
  `/events/feed.xml`. Cleaner, independently cacheable, one query per feed.
- **Extend the blog feed**: only when the user explicitly wants a single combined
  feed. Merge the extra items into the existing `app/feed.xml/route.ts` `items`
  array before `generateRssFeed`.

## The helper contract — `lib/utils/rss.ts`

```ts
generateRssFeed({
  title: string,
  link: string,        // channel homepage for this feed
  description: string,
  feedUrl: string,     // absolute URL of THIS feed (self link)
  items: RssFeedItem[],
})
// RssFeedItem: { title, link, description?, pubDate?, authors?, category? }
```

`pubDate` is parsed with `new Date(...)`, so pass an ISO date string. `authors`
becomes `<dc:creator>` entries. Always return `rssErrorResponse()` from a `catch`.

## Identify the variant

Look at `lib/integrations/sanity/queries.ts`:

- **Standard Sanity** — content types are top-level documents (like `article`).
  Use `getBaseUrl` from `lib/utils/url.ts` and build paths inline
  (`` `${baseUrl}/blog/${slug}` ``). Only `getBaseUrl` is guaranteed here: the base
  templates ship their own `lib/utils/url.ts` and the integration is copied with
  `overwrite: false`, so don't rely on extra exports like `getPageUrl`.
- **Page builder** — collection entries are their own document types (like
  `blogPost`), declared in `lib/integrations/sanity/collections.ts`, which also
  builds their paths (`getCollectionEntryPath`, `getBlogPostPath`). URL helpers
  live in `lib/utils/sitemap.ts` (`getSitemapBaseUrl`, `getPageUrl`).

## Steps

1. **Query** — add a GROQ query to `lib/integrations/sanity/queries.ts` (wrap with
   `defineQuery` so typegen types it). Select the fields you'll map: title, slug
   (or `resolvedSlug`), a date, an author, and `metadata` (for `noIndex`).
2. **Route** — create `app/<type>/feed.xml/route.ts` with
   `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`, guard on a null `client`, fetch in a
   `try/catch`, filter out `metadata?.noIndex`, map docs to `RssFeedItem`, return
   `generateRssFeed(...)`.
3. **Register the path in the CLI** — if you're editing the *basement-cli source*

import { generateRssFeed, rssErrorResponse } from "@/lib/utils/rss";
import { getBaseUrl } from "@/lib/utils/url";

export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";

  const baseUrl = getBaseUrl();

The repo's copy wins. If you loaded this file from a machine-wide folder

Typecheck and build pass on a block that looks broken. Screenshots are how a
reviewer, and a designer, see what actually changed without running the app.

the call was. A designer decides.

environment variables and the publish webhook live in the README — read it too.

This is a **Next.js + Sanity page builder**: page URLs are managed in Sanity,
not in code, and a single catch-all route `[[...slug]]` renders every page.

their own document types with code routes.

Studio with a slug, not a directory. `app/(content)/[[...slug]]/page.tsx`
resolves every one of them; a hand-written route shadows that resolver and
becomes a URL no editor can see, move or delete. The only things that belong in
`app/` are non-page endpoints — the Studio, API handlers, sitemap, feed, and
`app/components`, the Studio's live block preview: it renders fixtures rather
than content, is gated to Studio embeds by `isStudioEmbed()` and is `noindex`.

**Collection routes are the exception.** A collection is declared once in
`lib/integrations/sanity/collections.ts` (document type, `basePath`, taxonomy)
and owns the routes under its `basePath` — the blog's posts render from
`app/(content)/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`. Its entries are `blogPost` documents, not
`page`s with a block, and the route folder must match the collection's
`basePath`. Build URLs to an entry with `getCollectionEntryPath`, never by hand.
A `page` whose URL sits directly under a `basePath` still renders through the
collection route when no entry has that slug; an entry with the same slug wins,
and the Studio flags the collision on both documents. Entries are linkable like
pages (`pageReference`), and appear in the sitemap, `sitemap.md`, the markdown
route and Presentation.

**The blog's listing is code, not pages.** The Blog Index (`/blog`) is a pinned
`page` holding the **Blog Posts Directory** block, which only that page may use
(`onlyOnPageIds` in `page-builder-config.ts`). `/blog/page/<n>`,
`/blog/category/<slug>` and `/blog/category/<slug>/page/<n>` are code routes
that reuse the directory; never create pages for categories. A category's
heading, description and SEO live on the `blogCategory` document, categories
without posts are hidden and 404, and page 1 always redirects to the
unnumbered URL. Build these URLs with `getBlogDirectoryPath`.

It runs with [Cache Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents)
(`cacheComponents: true`), so every Sanity read sits behind a `'use cache'`
boundary and lands in the static shell. Nothing is time-based — the publish
webhook is what invalidates. A new read that isn't cached or wrapped in
`<Suspense>` takes its whole route out of the static shell, so keep the
boundaries where they are unless you mean to move them.

## Page-builder blocks

**Blocks are inline objects, never documents.** A placement belongs to exactly
one page, so the page's `pageBuilder` array stores the block itself and nothing
is dereferenced at read time. Don't reintroduce a block-as-document with a
reference member — that model was removed deliberately: no block was ever
reused, and it cost a hop on every read plus a second id to address.

**A block is `defineBlock` + a registry entry.** Define the schema with
`defineBlock` (`lib/integrations/sanity/schemas/shared/block.ts`), never
`defineType` — it implies `type: "object"` and appends **Anchor ID** and
**Presentation Mode** for you. The array member's type name *is* the block's
`_type`, so the registry, the insert menu and the fixture library all key off
the same string. Register the component in
`components/page-builder/registry.tsx`; the renderer is driven by that map, so
there is no switch to extend.

Both halves are enforced, not documented: the registry's key set is typed as
exactly `PageBuilderDocumentType`, so a block registered in
`page-builder-config.ts` without an entry there — or an entry there for a block
that was never registered — is a typecheck error.

**Every block declares two orthogonal axes** in `page-builder-config.ts`:
`pageTypes` (which page documents may host it — drives validation) and
`category` (what the block structurally is, one of `componentCategories` —
drives the insert menu; `misc` only when nothing else fits). Never collapse them
into one field: that is what made the menu a single flat list.

**And a fixture.** A block isn't done until `components/page-builder/library.ts`
has an entry for it: a stand-in value typed as the block's query result, plus a
one-line note. That entry is the block's preview everywhere — the live pane in
the insert menu, its row in Studio → Components, and the `/components` route,
all rendered by the production renderer. Without one the picker just says the
component has no preview.

**Never hardcode vertical padding in a block component.** The renderer wraps
each block in `<Section>` (`components/page-builder/section.tsx`), which owns
the `<section>` element, the anchor `id`, `scroll-mt` and the responsive padding
top/bottom. A block component returns its content only — no outer `<section>`,
no `py-*` / `pt-*` / `pb-*` on its root. Internal gaps between a block's own
parts are fine.

**Every block sits on the page grid.** `Section` renders its children inside
`b-layout-grid`: 4 columns, 12 from `tablet-lg`, a 16px gutter and margin, at
most 1240px wide (`--columns`, `--gap`, `--safe`, `--layout-max-width` in
`lib/styles/global.css`). A grid item spans one column unless told otherwise,
so a block's root always declares its span — `col-span-full`, plus
`tablet-lg:col-span-*` / `col-start-*` to narrow it. Never set `max-w-*`,
`mx-auto` or `px-*` to size a block; a nested layout is a `<Grid subgrid>` or a
full-width `<Grid>` (`components/layout/grid`), so it lines up with the page.
Header, footer and anything outside a `Section` sit in a `<Container>`
(`components/layout/container`). Breakpoints are the basement scale —
`mobile`, `tablet`, `tablet-lg`, `desktop`, `desktop-large`; `sm:`, `md:`,
`lg:`, `xl:` and `2xl:` don't exist and compile to nothing.

**Never hardcode px for section spacing either.** The scale lives in the Studio
at **Layout → Spacing Scale**, where editors add or rename steps and mark one as
the default, and it reaches the page as CSS custom properties. `Section` only
references `var(--section-space-<key>, var(--section-space-default, 2.5rem))`.

**An empty Anchor ID is generated from the block's title** (`headline` /
`heading` / `teaserHeading` / `title` / `label` — never `internalTitle`, which is
Studio-only) and de-duplicated per page. Name your block's headline field one of
those and anchor links work for free.

Declare `isEmpty` in the registry when a block can be left unfilled — the
renderer then skips the block *and* its `<Section>`, so it leaves no padded gap
and claims no anchor id. Don't early-return `null` from the component instead;
the renderer has to know before it wraps anything.

Full recipe and a checklist for a new block: the `page-builder-block` skill, or
the "Page-builder blocks" section of the README.

## Sanity

- Everything Sanity lives in `lib/integrations/sanity/`.
- Schemas use `defineType` / `defineField` / `defineArrayMember` (blocks use
  `defineBlock`). GROQ queries are `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` and wrapped in
  `defineQuery`.
- **Regenerate types after any schema or query change:** `bun sanity:typegen`,
  and commit the result in the same PR. Never hand-edit `sanity.types.ts`.
- The page query spreads `...` for non-gated blocks, so new block fields flow
  through on their own — except `gatedContent`, whose GROQ branch lists fields
  explicitly in `lib/integrations/sanity/queries.ts`. Add fields there by hand.
- Read through `sanityFetch` / `fetchSanity`, not a bare client, so the
  draft-mode perspective and cache tags are applied.
- Publishing a document must invalidate what renders it. Layout singletons are
  listed in `SANITY_LAYOUT_TAGS`; a new one that isn't there serves stale.
- Add `data-sanity` attributes where visual editing should reach.
- Nested layouts (e.g. `app/studio/layout.tsx`) must NOT render `<html>` or
  `<body>` — the root layout already provides them.

## React and Next.js

- **React Compiler is on.** Do not write `useMemo`, `useCallback` or
  `React.memo`. The one exception is `useRef` to instantiate an object once:

  ```tsx
  const instanceRef = useRef<SomeClass | null>(null)
  if (!instanceRef.current) instanceRef.current = new SomeClass()
  ```

- React 19: refs are regular props, so no `forwardRef` (a lint rule enforces it).
- **Never call `headers()`, `cookies()`, `draftMode()` or read `searchParams` in
  a root layout** — it takes the whole page out of the prerender. Detect the
  route with `useSelectedLayoutSegment()` in a `"use client"` wrapper, and put
  draft-mode / visual-editing behaviour in a child component with its own
  `<Suspense>` boundary.
- Use `@/components/ui/image` rather than `next/image` directly, and
  `@/components/ui/sanity-image` for Sanity assets.
- Compose classNames with `cn` from `@/lib/styles/cn`.
- Import with the `@/` alias; relative parent imports are a lint error.
- Gate debug UI behind `process.env.NODE_ENV === "development"` — it is not
  stripped in production otherwise.

## House rules

- **Bun only.** `bun install`, `bun run <script>`, `bunx`. Never npm, pnpm or
  yarn — a second lockfile next to `bun.lock` is how the versions drift.
- **Don't add a dependency without asking.** Check `bun info <package>` and the
  current docs first.
<!-- bsmnt:if dotenvx -->
- **Secrets are encrypted at rest with dotenvx.** Never put a real secret in
  plaintext in a committed env file — gitleaks blocks the commit. Use
  `bun env:set KEY value` (`--plain` for trivial config and `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`).
  The `manage-env` skill has the full procedure.
<!-- bsmnt:endif -->
- **Verify before claiming done:**

  ```bash
  bun sanity:typegen && bun typecheck && bun lint && bun run build && bun knip
  ```

  (`bun run build`, not `bun build` — the bare form is Bun's bundler.) Say what
  you ran and what it printed; don't report success you haven't seen.
- **Before a commit or PR, or when told to ship, check the `launch-ready`
  skill's rules against the diff.** Run all of them when asked whether the site
  is ready to launch.

## Code

- **No code comments.** Make the code say it: clear names, small functions,
  types that describe the value. Don't add comments, docstrings,
  commented-out code or `TODO`s. The one exception is a tool directive that
  needs one, such as `biome-ignore` with its reason.
- **No tests.** Don't add test files, test runners, `test` scripts or CI test
  steps. Prove a change with typecheck, lint, build and the app in the
  browser; guard a recurring mistake with a type or a lint rule.

## Pull requests

The skills named here (`pr-risk`, `visual-proof`) are plain markdown, kept
in this repo under `.agents/skills/` (linked from `.claude/skills/`);
`bsmnt update review` brings them up to date. The repo's copy wins: an agent
can load an older machine-wide one from `~/.claude/skills/` or
`~/.agents/skills/` first, so when that happens, follow
`.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` instead. If your agent doesn't load skills,
open that `SKILL.md` and follow it directly. Same for `REVIEW.md`.

- **Assess risk before opening a PR.** Run the `pr-risk` skill on the diff and
  paste its `## Risk` block into the PR body: score, lane, the one safety fact
  and its evidence. A PR without it is not ready for review. Run the same
  assessment when reviewing someone else's change.
- Auth and secrets, and CI or review-policy files, require human review
  whatever the score. Everything else follows the score: design and visual
  changes, brand, design tokens, UI copy, SEO metadata (page titles and
  descriptions, JSON-LD and sitemap), schema, query, API and dependency
  changes.
- **Taste calls need a designer's eye.** Layout, spacing, typography,
  responsive trade-offs, motion, image crops, and anything the design file
  doesn't show can't be fully verified by an agent. Bring the evidence and
  name the call; a designer decides.
- Keep PRs small. If one has to exceed ~200 changed lines (lockfiles don't
  count), say why in the PR body.
- **Fill every section of the PR template**: Summary, Testing (what you ran and
  what it printed, plus mobile and desktop screenshots for anything a user can
  see — the `visual-proof` skill captures and attaches them), Risk, and How to
  revert (the exact way back, or say there is none).
- **Review rounds are capped by lane** (the `pr-risk` skill picks it): fast 1,
  standard 2, deep 3. After the first round, review only the new diff. At the
  cap, stop and rethink the approach instead of pushing another fix.
- **When reviewing**, follow `REVIEW.md`. Tag each finding Important, Nit or
  Pre-existing, with a `file:line`. Name the class of problem so it gets fixed
  in one pass, and don't repeat a finding already raised. Skip nits that would
  cost the author a whole new commit.
- **Resolve every thread**: fix it, or close it with a short reason.
- **Add `fast` last, never when requesting review.** Finish every required
  review first, including a fresh-context agent pass on the final commit.
  Record its SHA and clean result in the PR. Only then may a fast-lane PR
  get the label: allowlisted docs, or, when `.github/fast-lane.json` sets
  `riskGate`, a PR whose Risk block says score under 50, lane fast and
  designer's eye not needed. It attests that review is done; CI does not run
  another reviewer. Follow `.github/FAST_LANE.md`. New commits invalidate it.
  Never label standard/deep work, unresolved findings or taste calls `fast`.
  The fast lane needs no human approval and is only an extra path for those
  changes; every other PR follows the normal review flow.
- An agent's approval never stands in for a required human one, and a new
  commit after approval needs a fresh look.
- The default branch is protected: changes land only through a PR with green
  CI and every thread resolved. Never push to it directly or try to bypass it.

  rule, a skill, or a line in this file.

references `var(--section-space-<key>, var(--section-space-default, 2.5rem))`.

**An empty Anchor ID is generated from the block's title** (`headline` /
`heading` / `teaserHeading` / `title` / `label` — never `internalTitle`, which is
Studio-only) and de-duplicated per page. Name your block's headline field one of
those and anchor links work for free.

Declare `isEmpty` in the registry when a block can be left unfilled — the
renderer then skips the block *and* its `<Section>`, so it leaves no padded gap
and claims no anchor id. Don't early-return `null` from the component instead;
the renderer has to know before it wraps anything.

Full recipe and a checklist for a new block: the `page-builder-block` skill, or
the "Page-builder blocks" section of the README.

## Sanity

- Everything Sanity lives in `lib/integrations/sanity/`.
- Schemas use `defineType` / `defineField` / `defineArrayMember` (blocks use
  `defineBlock`). GROQ queries are `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` and wrapped in
  `defineQuery`.
- **Regenerate types after any schema or query change:** `bun sanity:typegen`,
  and commit the result in the same PR. Never hand-edit `sanity.types.ts`.
- The page query spreads `...` for non-gated blocks, so new block fields flow
  through on their own — except `gatedContent`, whose GROQ branch lists fields
  explicitly in `lib/integrations/sanity/queries.ts`. Add fields there by hand.
- Read through `sanityFetch` / `fetchSanity`, not a bare client, so the
  draft-mode perspective and cache tags are applied.
- Publishing a document must invalidate what renders it. Layout singletons are
  listed in `SANITY_LAYOUT_TAGS`; a new one that isn't there serves stale.
- Add `data-sanity` attributes where visual editing should reach.
- Nested layouts (e.g. `app/studio/layout.tsx`) must NOT render `<html>` or
  `<body>` — the root layout already provides them.

## React and Next.js

- **React Compiler is on.** Do not write `useMemo`, `useCallback` or
  `React.memo`. The one exception is `useRef` to instantiate an object once:

  ```tsx
  const instanceRef = useRef<SomeClass | null>(null)
  if (!instanceRef.current) instanceRef.current = new SomeClass()
  ```

- React 19: refs are regular props, so no `forwardRef` (a lint rule enforces it).
- **Never call `headers()`, `cookies()`, `draftMode()` or read `searchParams` in
  a root layout** — it takes the whole page out of the prerender. Detect the
  route with `useSelectedLayoutSegment()` in a `"use client"` wrapper, and put
  draft-mode / visual-editing behaviour in a child component with its own
  `<Suspense>` boundary.
- Use `@/components/ui/image` rather than `next/image` directly, and
  `@/components/ui/sanity-image` for Sanity assets.
- Compose classNames with `cn` from `@/lib/styles/cn`.
- Import with the `@/` alias; relative parent imports are a lint error.
- Gate debug UI behind `process.env.NODE_ENV === "development"` — it is not
  stripped in production otherwise.

## House rules

- **Bun only.** `bun install`, `bun run <script>`, `bunx`. Never npm, pnpm or
  yarn — a second lockfile next to `bun.lock` is how the versions drift.
- **Don't add a dependency without asking.** Check `bun info <package>` and the
  current docs first.
<!-- bsmnt:if dotenvx -->
- **Secrets are encrypted at rest with dotenvx.** Never put a real secret in
  plaintext in a committed env file — gitleaks blocks the commit. Use
  `bun env:set KEY value` (`--plain` for trivial config and `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`).
  The `manage-env` skill has the full procedure.
<!-- bsmnt:endif -->
- **Verify before claiming done:**

  ```bash
  bun sanity:typegen && bun typecheck && bun lint && bun run build && bun knip
  ```

  (`bun run build`, not `bun build` — the bare form is Bun's bundler.) Say what
  you ran and what it printed; don't report success you haven't seen.
- **Before a commit or PR, or when told to ship, check the `launch-ready`
  skill's rules against the diff.** Run all of them when asked whether the site
  is ready to launch.

## Code

- **No code comments.** Make the code say it: clear names, small functions,
  types that describe the value. Don't add comments, docstrings,
  commented-out code or `TODO`s. The one exception is a tool directive that
  needs one, such as `biome-ignore` with its reason.
- **No tests.** Don't add test files, test runners, `test` scripts or CI test
  steps. Prove a change with typecheck, lint, build and the app in the
  browser; guard a recurring mistake with a type or a lint rule.

## Pull requests

The skills named here (`pr-risk`, `visual-proof`) are plain markdown, kept
in this repo under `.agents/skills/` (linked from `.claude/skills/`);
`bsmnt update review` brings them up to date. The repo's copy wins: an agent
can load an older machine-wide one from `~/.claude/skills/` or
`~/.agents/skills/` first, so when that happens, follow
`.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` instead. If your agent doesn't load skills,
open that `SKILL.md` and follow it directly. Same for `REVIEW.md`.

- **Assess risk before opening a PR.** Run the `pr-risk` skill on the diff and

  and its evidence. A PR without it is not ready for review. Run the same
  assessment when reviewing someone else's change.
- Auth and secrets, and CI or review-policy files, require human review

  descriptions, JSON-LD and sitemap), schema, query, API and dependency

  responsive trade-offs, motion, image crops, and anything the design file
  doesn't show can't be fully verified by an agent. Bring the evidence and
  name the call; a designer decides.

  count), say why in the PR body.

# Page Builder Template (Cache Components)

Next.js + Sanity CMS page builder architecture. Page URLs are managed in Sanity, not in code; the blog is a content collection with its own routes.

This is the [Cache Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents)
variant: `cacheComponents: true`, so every Sanity read sits behind a `'use cache'`
boundary and lands in the static shell, and `cacheLife` runs on a ~1-year window.
Nothing is time-based — the publish webhook is what invalidates, and
`<SanityLive />` only runs in draft mode. See "Content invalidation" below; without
that webhook, published changes never reach the deployed site.

## Getting Started

```bash
bun dev
```

## Architecture

- Single catch-all route `[[...slug]]` handles all pages
- Sanity page builder with composable content blocks
- Editor-owned vertical spacing scale and per-block anchor links
- Blog as a content collection: `blogPost` documents rendered by `app/(content)/blog/[slug]`, declared in `lib/integrations/sanity/collections.ts`
- Blog Posts Directory on the Blog Index page, with static category pages (`/blog/category/<slug>`) and pagination (`/blog/page/<n>`) generated in code
- Visual editing and live preview support

## Page-builder blocks

A block is two halves — a schema type and a React component — and each half has
one place that makes it a block rather than an ordinary object type or a loose
component. Use them and Anchor ID, Presentation Mode and the spacing scale come
for free.

Blocks are **inline objects** in the page's `pageBuilder` array, never documents
and never referenced: a placement belongs to exactly one page, so the block
lives on that page and nothing is dereferenced at read time.

**Define the schema with `defineBlock`, never `defineType`**
(`lib/integrations/sanity/schemas/shared/block.ts`). It implies
`type: "object"` and appends two fields to every block:

- **Anchor ID** — optional. Left empty, the anchor is generated from the block's
  own title at render time (`headline` / `heading` / `teaserHeading` / `title` /
  `label` — never `internalTitle`, which is Studio-only) and de-duplicated per
  page, so two blocks with the same heading get `-2`. A value typed by hand
  always wins, and the Studio shows the generated one as the placeholder. Link
  to it as `/<page>#<anchor>`.
- **Presentation Mode** — padding top and bottom, each picked from the shared
  spacing scale. No free-form px. A block that never touches it follows whichever
  step is marked as the default.

Blocks that declare `groups` get a **Presentation** tab for both fields
automatically — don't list it in `groups` yourself.

**Register the component in `components/page-builder/registry.tsx`.** One entry
per block, keyed by schema type; the renderer is driven by that map, so there is
no switch to extend. `isEmpty` declares when a block has nothing to show — the
renderer then skips the block *and* its `<Section>`, so an unfilled block leaves
no padded gap behind and claims no anchor id. The registry's key set is typed as
exactly `PageBuilderDocumentType`, so a block registered in one place and not the
other is a typecheck error.

**Never hardcode vertical padding in a block component.** The renderer wraps each
block in `<Section>` (`components/page-builder/section.tsx`), which owns the
`<section>` element, the anchor `id`, `scroll-mt` and the padding. A block
component returns its content only — no outer `<section>`, no `py-*` / `pt-*` /
`pb-*` on its root. Internal gaps between a block's own parts are fine.

**Every block ships a fixture in `components/page-builder/library.ts`**: a
stand-in value typed as the block's query result, plus a one-line note. It is
the block's only preview, and it is rendered by the production renderer at
`/components` — a route the Studio embeds in an iframe, so the insert menu and
**Components** in the Studio show the real block rather than a screenshot. The
route is gated to Studio embeds and `noindex`; a block with no entry simply has
no preview.

### The spacing scale is content, not code

Editors own it at **Layout → Spacing Scale**: a list of steps, each with a name
and px per breakpoint (mobile / tablet / desktop, empty reuses Desktop), one
marked as the default. Ticking a second step as default unticks the previous, so
there is always exactly one. Add a "Hero 120px" step and it shows up in every
block's dropdown, no deploy.

- Blocks store the step's `_key`, so renaming a step breaks nothing and a deleted
  step degrades to the default instead of breaking the page.
- The list arrives seeded with the built-in five (XS 16 · SM 24 · **MD 32,
  default** · LG 48 · XL 80, from `schemas/shared/spacing.ts`), which also apply
  as the fallback if you empty it. Hit **"Add the built-in steps"** in the field
  to get them back as editable rows.
- Values reach the page as CSS custom properties injected server-side by
  `components/layout/spacing-scale/`, one `--section-space-<key>` per step plus
  `--section-space-default`, re-declared inside the `768px` and `1440px` media
  queries. `Section` only ever references
  `var(--section-space-<key>, var(--section-space-default, 2.5rem))`, so an
  unknown key degrades instead of breaking.

Under Cache Components the scale is read inside a `'use cache'` boundary and
prerenders into the static shell alongside the rest of the chrome, so the first
paint already carries the variables; draft mode streams the editor's copy behind
a `<Suspense>` that falls back to the built-in steps.
- `spacingSettings` is a layout singleton, so publishing it busts the layout
  cache the same way navbar and footer do.

After a schema change run `bun sanity:typegen`. The page query spreads `...` for
non-gated blocks, so new fields flow through on their own — except
`gatedContent`, whose GROQ branch lists fields explicitly in
`lib/integrations/sanity/queries.ts`.

The bundled `page-builder-block` agent skill has the full recipe and a checklist
for adding a new block.

## Sanity Dashboard (Studio in an iframe)

The Studio at `/studio` can be embedded in the Sanity Dashboard
(`https://www.sanity.io/@<org>/studio/<appId>/<workspace>`), which loads it in an
iframe from `www.sanity.io`. Three things have to be true for that to work:

1. **Headers.** `next.config.ts` already exempts `/studio/:path*` from the
   site-wide `X-Frame-Options` / `frame-ancestors 'self'` headers, sending
   `frame-ancestors 'self' https://*.sanity.io` there instead and dropping
   `X-Frame-Options` entirely for that path (it has no "allow this origin"
   form — it must be absent, not overridden). Nothing to do here unless
   you've hand-edited `headers()`.
2. **Bridge script.** Already wired in: `next-sanity/studio`'s `NextStudio`
   re-exports `NextStudioWithBridge`, which renders the
   `core.sanity-cdn.com/bridge.js` tag the Dashboard needs. Don't hand-roll
   that script tag, and don't switch the Studio route to
   `next-sanity/studio/client-component` (the bridge-less variant).
3. **Registered URL.** In [Sanity Manage](https://sanity.io/manage), the
   Studio application's URL must be the **full path**
   (`https://example.com/studio`), not just the domain. This can't be set
   from code — either click through Manage, or run
   `sanity deploy --external --url https://example.com/studio --yes` from
   `lib/integrations/sanity`. Writing it via the API needs the
   `sanity.project.deployStudio` grant, which read/write tokens don't have.

## Page-builder blocks

A block is two halves — a schema type and a React component — and each half has
one place that makes it a block rather than an ordinary object type or a loose
component. Use them and Anchor ID, Presentation Mode and the spacing scale come
for free.

Blocks are **inline objects** in the page's `pageBuilder` array, never documents
and never referenced: a placement belongs to exactly one page, so the block
lives on that page and nothing is dereferenced at read time.

**Define the schema with `defineBlock`, never `defineType`**
(`lib/integrations/sanity/schemas/shared/block.ts`). It implies
`type: "object"` and appends two fields to every block:

- **Anchor ID** — optional. Left empty, the anchor is generated from the block's
  own title at render time (`headline` / `heading` / `teaserHeading` / `title` /
  `label` — never `internalTitle`, which is Studio-only) and de-duplicated per
  page, so two blocks with the same heading get `-2`. A value typed by hand
  always wins, and the Studio shows the generated one as the placeholder. Link
  to it as `/<page>#<anchor>`.
- **Presentation Mode** — padding top and bottom, each picked from the shared
  spacing scale. No free-form px. A block that never touches it follows whichever
  step is marked as the default.

Blocks that declare `groups` get a **Presentation** tab for both fields
automatically — don't list it in `groups` yourself.

**Register the component in `components/page-builder/registry.tsx`.** One entry
per block, keyed by schema type; the renderer is driven by that map, so there is
no switch to extend. `isEmpty` declares when a block has nothing to show — the
renderer then skips the block *and* its `<Section>`, so an unfilled block leaves
no padded gap behind and claims no anchor id. The registry's key set is typed as
exactly `PageBuilderDocumentType`, so a block registered in one place and not the
other is a typecheck error.

**Never hardcode vertical padding in a block component.** The renderer wraps each
block in `<Section>` (`components/page-builder/section.tsx`), which owns the
`<section>` element, the anchor `id`, `scroll-mt` and the padding. A block
component returns its content only — no outer `<section>`, no `py-*` / `pt-*` /
`pb-*` on its root. Internal gaps between a block's own parts are fine.

**Every block ships a fixture in `components/page-builder/library.ts`**: a
stand-in value typed as the block's query result, plus a one-line note. It is
the block's only preview, and it is rendered by the production renderer at
`/components` — a route the Studio embeds in an iframe, so the insert menu and
**Components** in the Studio show the real block rather than a screenshot. The
route is gated to Studio embeds and `noindex`; a block with no entry simply has
no preview.

### The spacing scale is content, not code

Editors own it at **Layout → Spacing Scale**: a list of steps, each with a name
and px per breakpoint (mobile / tablet / desktop, empty reuses Desktop), one
marked as the default. Ticking a second step as default unticks the previous, so
there is always exactly one. Add a "Hero 120px" step and it shows up in every
block's dropdown, no deploy.

- Blocks store the step's `_key`, so renaming a step breaks nothing and a deleted
  step degrades to the default instead of breaking the page.
- The list arrives seeded with the built-in five (XS 16 · SM 24 · **MD 32,
  default** · LG 48 · XL 80, from `schemas/shared/spacing.ts`), which also apply
  as the fallback if you empty it. Hit **"Add the built-in steps"** in the field
  to get them back as editable rows.
- Values reach the page as CSS custom properties injected server-side by
  `components/layout/spacing-scale/`, one `--section-space-<key>` per step plus
  `--section-space-default`, re-declared inside the `768px` and `1440px` media
  queries. `Section` only ever references
  `var(--section-space-<key>, var(--section-space-default, 2.5rem))`, so an
  unknown key degrades instead of breaking.
- `spacingSettings` is a layout singleton, so publishing it busts the layout
  cache the same way navbar and footer do.

After a schema change run `bun sanity:typegen`. The page query spreads `...` for
non-gated blocks, so new fields flow through on their own — except
`gatedContent`, whose GROQ branch lists fields explicitly in
`lib/integrations/sanity/queries.ts`.

for adding a new block.

Access Studio at `/studio` 2. Create content (Articles) 3. Click "Present" for visual editing ## Usage ### Fetching Data ```tsx import { sanityFetch } from 'next-sanity/live' import { ARTICLE_QUERY } from '@/lib/integrations/sanity/queries' export default async function Page({ params }) { const { data } = await sanityFetch({ query: ARTICLE_QUERY, params: { slug: params.slug } }) return } ``` ### Build-time Data Fetching For `generateStaticParams` or other build-time functions, use the client directly: ```tsx import { client } from '@/lib/integrations/sanity/client' import { ALL_ARTICLES_QUERY } from '@/lib/integrations/sanity/queries' export async function generateStaticParams() { if (!client) return [] const data = await client.fetch(ALL_ARTICLES_QUERY) return data.map((item) => ({ slug: item.slug?.current ?? '' })) } ``` ### Visual Editing Add `data-sanity` attributes for visual editing: ```tsx import { RichText } from '@/lib/integrations/sanity/components/rich-text' function MyComponent({ data }) { return (

{data.title}

) } ``` ### Image Handling ```tsx import { urlForImage } from '@/lib/integrations/sanity/utils/image' import { SanityImage } from '@/components/ui/sanity-image' // Option 1: Using urlForImage utility // Option 2: Using SanityImage component ``` ### SEO Metadata ```tsx import { generateSanityMetadata } from '@/lib/utils/metadata' export async function generateMetadata({ params }) { const { data } = await sanityFetch({ query: ARTICLE_QUERY, params }) return generateSanityMetadata({ document: data, url: `/blog/${params.slug}` }) } ``` ## Creating New Content Types 1. **Create schema** in `schemaTypes/`: ```typescript import { defineField, defineType } from 'sanity' export const landing = defineType({ name: 'landing', type: 'document', fields: [ defineField({ name: 'title', type: 'string' }), defineField({ name: 'slug', type: 'slug', options: { source: 'title' } }), defineField({ name: 'content', type: 'richText' }), ], }) ``` 2. **Add to schema index** in `schemaTypes/index.ts` 3. **Create query** in `queries.ts` 4. **Create page** in `app/` ## Caching - **Draft mode**: Uses `cache: 'no-store'` automatically - **Published content**: ISR with `revalidate: 3600` - All queries use `cacheSignal()` for automatic cleanup See [ARCHITECTURE.md](../../../ARCHITECTURE.md) for cache gotchas. ## Sanity Dashboard (Studio in an iframe) The Studio at `/studio` can be embedded in the Sanity Dashboard (`https://www.sanity.io/@/studio//`), which loads it in an iframe from `www.sanity.io`. Three things have to be true for that to work: 1. **Headers.** `next.config.ts` already exempts `/studio/:path*` from the site-wide `X-Frame-Options` / `frame-ancestors 'self'` headers, sending `frame-ancestors 'self' https://*.sanity.io` there instead and dropping `X-Frame-Options` entirely for that path (it has no "allow this origin" form — it must be absent, not overridden). Nothing to do here unless you've hand-edited `headers()`. 2. **Bridge script.** Already wired in: `next-sanity/studio`'s `NextStudio` re-exports `NextStudioWithBridge`, which renders the `core.sanity-cdn.com/bridge.js` tag the Dashboard needs. Don't hand-roll that script tag, and don't switch the Studio route to `next-sanity/studio/client-component` (the bridge-less variant). 3. **Registered URL.** In [Sanity Manage](https://sanity.io/manage), the Studio application's URL must be the **full path** (`https://example.com/studio`), not just the domain. This can't be set from code — either click through Manage, or run `sanity deploy --external --url https://example.com/studio --yes` from `lib/integrations/sanity`. # Ketch consent integration (CMP)

[Ketch](https://app.ketch.com) is the consent management platform. It decides,
per visitor and per region, whether the site may run analytics or marketing
trackers. **No tracking script may fire without asking it first.**

## 1. Environment

Both codes are public — they appear in the boot URL in the page source — so
they go in as plain values:

```bash
NEXT_PUBLIC_KETCH_ORG_CODE=
NEXT_PUBLIC_KETCH_PROPERTY_CODE=
```

Get them from the Ketch dashboard at https://app.ketch.com, or read them out
of the boot URL if all you have is the raw `<script>` snippet:

```
https://global.ketchcdn.com/web/v3/config/<org>/<property>/boot.js
```

## 2. Checking consent

One helper, always — categories are `essential`, `analytics`, `marketing`:

```tsx
const { hasConsent } = useConsent() // @/lib/integrations/ketch/use-consent

useEffect(() => {
  if (!hasConsent("analytics")) return
  const tracker = start()
  return () => tracker.stop() // this is what makes revocation work
}, [hasConsent])
```

It returns `false` until Ketch resolves, so a tracker written this way cannot
fire early. Never read `window.ketch`, cookies or `localStorage` directly —
outside React, subscribe to `consentStore` from `./consent-store` instead.

Map each tracker to a category in `categories.ts`'s `TRACKER_CONSENT_CATEGORY`
so the mapping lives in one place and is reviewable. See the
`ketch-consent-check` agent skill for the full walkthrough (loader shape,
cleanup, SDKs without teardown).

Preferences are reachable from `<ConsentPreferencesButton />` in the footer
and from Ketch's own floating button (kept by default, since the footer entry
point isn't guaranteed on every project this integration is added to). Hide
the floating button in `ketch-experience.css` only once another entry point
is confirmed to exist — see the `ketch-consent-setup` skill's UI reference.

## 3. Region behaviour

Ketch resolves a jurisdiction from the visitor's IP — nothing to configure in
code. EEA/UK/Switzerland, California and Quebec are opt-in (nothing runs until
the visitor accepts); Canada and 14 US states are opt-out (on until refused);
everywhere else falls to `default`, which is notice-only. Because the helper
stays denied until Ketch confirms, the site's own trackers wait for the
record in every region.

In a notice-only region the purpose toggles render locked as "Always Active"
and the Accept/Reject buttons have nothing to change — that is the
jurisdiction's configuration, not a bug.

Also true for opt-out regions: consent is granted automatically with no
banner interaction, so the banner won't come back on reload either. To test
the real Accept/Reject UI from a region that defaults to notice-only, append
`?ketch_jurisdiction=gdpr` to the URL — see the `ketch-consent-setup` skill's
UI reference for the full mechanism.

# HubSpot Forms integration

Agnostic, reusable HubSpot Forms embed. The core (`form.tsx`, `embed.tsx`,
`forms.ts`, `form-selection.ts`, `hubspot-form.css`) has **no CMS dependency**
and adds **no runtime packages** — it loads HubSpot's official forms script and
styles the injected DOM with self-contained, themeable CSS.

## 1. Environment

Create a HubSpot **private app** with the `forms` and
`account-info.security.read` scopes, then add its token to `.env.local`:

```bash
HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN=pat-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
```

The token is only read server-side (in `forms.ts`); it is never exposed to the
client.

## 2. Render a form

If you already know the form, pass `portalId` / `formId` / `region` directly:

```tsx
import { HubSpotForm } from "@/lib/integrations/hubspot/form"

export function Contact() {
  return (
    <HubSpotForm
      portalId="1234567"
      formId="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
      region="na1"
    />
  )
}
```

`region` is the portal's data-hosting location (`na1`, `eu1`, …).

## 3. Theming

By default the form inherits the **basement starter** design tokens, so it
matches the surrounding site with no extra work:

| `--hs-*` token | Maps to (fallback) |
| --- | --- |
| `--hs-surface` | `--color-primary` (`#ffffff`) |
| `--hs-text` / `--hs-text-strong` | `--color-secondary` (`#18181b`) |
| `--hs-accent` | `--color-contrast` (`#ff4d00`) |
| `--hs-muted` | `--color-gray-400` (`#858585`) |
| `--hs-font-sans` | `--font-sans` → `--font-mono` → system |

Light/dark follows the host's `[data-theme]` automatically (via
`--color-primary` / `--color-secondary`). Outside the starter, the fallbacks
render a clean light theme.

Override any token from a parent scope to customize:

```css
.my-section {
  --hs-accent: #487cff;
  --hs-surface: #0a0a0a;
  --hs-text: #ededed;
  --hs-radius: 8px;
}
```

## 4. Listing forms programmatically

`getHubSpotFormOptions()` (from `forms.ts`) returns every published form in the
portal as `{ label, value, renderRawHtml }`. Each `value` is a JSON-encoded
selection — decode it with `decodeHubSpotFormSelection` and spread it into
`<HubSpotForm />`.

## 5. Optional: Sanity Studio form picker

When this integration is added to a project that already has Sanity, a
`sanity/` folder ships alongside the core with a Studio picker:

- `sanity/form-field.ts` — a ready-to-use `hubspotFormField` (`defineField`)
- `sanity/form-select-input.tsx` — the `<Autocomplete>` input it uses
- `sanity/form-block.ts` — a sample `hubspotFormBlock` document type

Wire the field into any schema:

```ts
import { defineType } from "sanity"
import { hubspotFormField } from "@/lib/integrations/hubspot/sanity/form-field"

export const contactBlock = defineType({
  name: "contactBlock",
  type: "object",
  fields: [hubspotFormField],
})
```

Or register the sample block by adding `hubspotFormBlock` to your schema's
document list, then render it (see the example in `sanity/form-block.ts`).

## 6. Use as a page-builder block

In a basement **Sanity page-builder** project, `hubspotFormBlock` can be a
selectable block. Adding this integration installs the
**`hubspot-pagebuilder-block`** agent skill — ask your coding agent to "wire the
HubSpot form into the page builder" and it makes the edits and verifies the
typecheck. To do it by hand:

1. `schemas/components/reusable/hubspot-form.ts` — re-declare the adapter
   through `defineBlock`, so the block is an inline object with Anchor ID and
   Presentation Mode; export it from `schemas/components/index.ts` and add it to
   `schema.types` in `schemas/index.ts`
2. `page-builder-config.ts` — add `"hubspotFormBlock"` to
   `PageBuilderDocumentType` and a `pageBuilderBlockMembers` entry with
   `pageTypes` and `category`
3. `components/page-builder/registry.tsx` — one entry keyed `hubspotFormBlock`
   that decodes `block.form` and renders `<HubSpotForm />`
4. `components/page-builder/library.ts` — a fixture entry, which is what the
   insert menu, Studio → Components and `/components` render
5. `bun run sanity:typegen && bun typecheck`

# Ashby job board integration Agnostic, reusable [Ashby](https://www.ashbyhq.com/) job-board reader. The core (`index.ts`, `normalize.ts`, `types.ts`) has **no CMS dependency** and adds **no runtime packages** — it reads Ashby's public Job Posting API and normalizes it into a stable `CareerJob[]`. Fetching is **server-only**: `getCareerJobs` uses `react`'s `cache` and Next.js `fetch` revalidation, so call it from a Server Component, Route Handler, or `generateMetadata` — never from a `"use client"` component. ## 1. Environment Ashby's job-board endpoint is public — no token or private app required. The only configuration is the board name, which is the slug in your board's URL (`https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/`): ```bash ASHBY_JOB_BOARD_NAME=your-board ``` The value is not a secret, so it can stay plaintext in the committed env file. It is only read server-side (in `env.ts`); it is never exposed to the client. You can also skip the variable entirely and pass the board name explicitly. `env.ts` resolves it once at module scope as `ashbyBoardName`, and `isAshbyConfigured()` in `lib/integrations/check-integration.ts` derives from that same value — so a "configured" check can never disagree with what `getCareerJobs` actually resolves. ## 2. Read the jobs ```tsx import { getCareerJobs } from "@/lib/integrations/ashby" export default async function Careers() { const jobs = await getCareerJobs() return (
    {jobs.map((job) => (
  • {job.title}
    • ))}
) } ``` Pass a board name to override `ASHBY_JOB_BOARD_NAME` (useful for multi-brand sites, or to render a second board on one page): ```tsx const jobs = await getCareerJobs("your-other-board") ``` `getCareerJobs` throws when the board name is missing or when Ashby responds with a non-2xx status. What you get `normalize.ts` tolerates both the current (`jobs`) and legacy (`jobPostings`) payload shapes, drops unlisted postings, and resolves each field from the several key spellings Ashby has used over time. # Review guidelines

For anyone reviewing a PR, agent or person, whatever tool runs the review.
Read it with the repo's `AGENTS.md`.

Find the bugs that would hurt users or mislead the next person. Skip the
rest. A review that flags ten nits and misses one stale-cache bug failed.

## Before you start

- Read the PR body. It must have **Summary**, **Testing**, **Risk** and **How
  to revert**. If one is missing or empty, that is your first finding.
- Use the `## Risk` block's lane for your depth and round limit. If the score
  looks wrong for the diff, say so and why.
- A fast-lane PR can merge on its Risk block's **Score**, **Lane** and
  **Designer's eye** lines. Check each against the diff. A forced category or a
  score that should be 50 or more means the PR is not fast: flag it as
  **Important**. A visual change still needs mobile and desktop screenshots,
  and a taste call still needs a designer.
- Check the proof, not the claim. "Tested locally" with no output is level 1
  evidence. A visual change without mobile and desktop screenshots is not
  ready.

## What counts as a failure

Flag these as **Important**:

- The change doesn't do what the PR says, or a bug fix patches the symptom
  instead of the root cause.
- It breaks something else: a caller, another consumer of the same data, a
  layout or style shared across pages.
- Stale data: caching or invalidation no longer covers what changed.
- Generated files (types, clients, schemas) left out of date in the same PR.
- A secret in plaintext, or an auth or permission check weakened.
- A broken user path: a dead link, a missing redirect, a page that renders
  empty, metadata or the sitemap dropping a page.
- Debug code or UI that ships to production.
- New code comments or tests: test files, test scripts or CI test steps.
- A rule in `AGENTS.md` broken.
- Docs that now lie: `AGENTS.md`, the README or a skill that no longer matches
  the code.

## Taste calls

Layout, spacing, typography, responsive behavior, motion, image crops, and any
"close enough to the design" call need a designer's eye. Don't approve or
reject them on your own. Check the screenshots exist, then flag:
"**Designer's eye**: <the call>".

## Don't flag

- Formatting and lint style. The linter already enforces it.
- Naming or structure preferences with no bug behind them.
- Generated files (only check they were regenerated), lockfiles, build output,
  or binary assets.
- Nits that would cost an agent author a whole new commit and review round.
  Leave them out.

## How to report

- Every finding gets a tag: **Important** (must fix before merge), **Nit**
  (optional, only if cheap), or **Pre-existing** (was already there, don't
  block the PR on it).
- Every finding gets a real `file:line`. Never guess a filename.
- Name the class of problem, so the author fixes every instance in one go.
- Start with a one-line summary: how many findings by tag, or a clear "No
  issues found."

## When to stop

- Round one reviews the full diff. Every round after that reviews only what
  changed since the last one.
- Never repeat a finding that was already raised or closed with a reason.
- Stop at the lane's cap: fast 1, standard 2, deep 3. At the cap, don't ask
  for another fix. Ask the author to rethink the approach, or hand it to a
  person.
- Your approval never replaces a required human one.

## Next.js + Sanity page builder

Applies when the repo is a Next.js + Sanity page builder (it has a
`sanity.config.ts` and `components/page-builder/`). Also flag as
**Important**:

- A one-off page hand-written under `app/`. Pages live in Sanity. A
  collection (a blog, for example) gets its own document type and route, and
  tooling routes like `/studio` and `/components` are fine.
- A block missing its registry entry or fixture, or a block root that renders
  its own `<section>` or vertical padding.
- Hardcoded px for section spacing instead of the spacing scale.
- A schema or query change without regenerated `sanity.types.ts` in the same
  PR, or a new `gatedContent` field missing from its explicit GROQ branch.
- A bare Sanity client instead of `sanityFetch` / `fetchSanity`, or a new
  layout singleton missing from `SANITY_LAYOUT_TAGS`. Both serve stale content.
- `headers()`, `cookies()`, `draftMode()` or `searchParams` in a root layout.
- `useMemo`, `useCallback`, `React.memo` or `forwardRef` (React Compiler is on).
- Debug UI that can reach production with no gate in front of it.

Don't flag anything inside `sanity.types.ts`. Only check it was regenerated.

Where a change also shows up: the sitemap, the RSS feed, JSON-LD and the
`/components` preview all read the same projections. A spread `...`
projection returns new fields to every consumer. Nav, footer and the spacing
scale touch every page.

Previewing a block: `/components?component=<blockType>` only renders inside
the Studio, so it 404s when opened directly. Open `/studio` first, then
navigate from that page (for example run
`location.href = "/components?component=featuresGrid"`).
