- A block missing its registry entry or fixture, or a block root that renders
  its own `<section>` or vertical padding.
- Hardcoded px for section spacing instead of the spacing scale.
- A schema or query change without regenerated `sanity.types.ts` in the same
  PR, or a new `gatedContent` field missing from its explicit GROQ branch.
- A bare Sanity client instead of `sanityFetch` / `fetchSanity`, or a new
  layout singleton missing from `SANITY_LAYOUT_TAGS`. Both serve stale content.
- `headers()`, `cookies()`, `draftMode()` or `searchParams` in a root layout.
- `useMemo`, `useCallback`, `React.memo` or `forwardRef` (React Compiler is on).
- Debug UI that can reach production with no gate in front of it.

Don't flag anything inside `sanity.types.ts`. Only check it was regenerated.

Where a change also shows up: the sitemap, the RSS feed, JSON-LD and the
`/components` preview all read the same projections. A spread `...`
projection returns new fields to every consumer. Nav, footer and the spacing
scale touch every page.

Previewing a block: `/components?component=<blockType>` only renders inside
the Studio, so it 404s when opened directly. Open `/studio` first, then
navigate from that page (for example run
`location.href = "/components?component=featuresGrid"`).

# Review guidelines

For anyone reviewing a PR, agent or person, whatever tool runs the review.
Read it with the repo's `AGENTS.md`.

Find the bugs that would hurt users or mislead the next person. Skip the
rest. A review that flags ten nits and misses one stale-cache bug failed.

## Before you start

- Read the PR body. It must have **Summary**, **Testing**, **Risk** and **How
  to revert**. If one is missing or empty, that is your first finding.
- Use the `## Risk` block's lane for your depth and round limit. If the score
  looks wrong for the diff, say so and why.
- A fast-lane PR can merge on its Risk block's **Score**, **Lane** and
  **Designer's eye** lines. Check each against the diff. A forced category or a
  score that should be 50 or more means the PR is not fast: flag it as
  **Important**. A visual change still needs mobile and desktop screenshots,
  and a taste call still needs a designer.
- Check the proof, not the claim. "Tested locally" with no output is level 1
  evidence. A visual change without mobile and desktop screenshots is not
  ready.

## What counts as a failure

Flag these as **Important**:

- The change doesn't do what the PR says, or a bug fix patches the symptom
  instead of the root cause.
- It breaks something else: a caller, another consumer of the same data, a
  layout or style shared across pages.
- Stale data: caching or invalidation no longer covers what changed.
- Generated files (types, clients, schemas) left out of date in the same PR.
- A secret in plaintext, or an auth or permission check weakened.
- A broken user path: a dead link, a missing redirect, a page that renders
  empty, metadata or the sitemap dropping a page.
- Debug code or UI that ships to production.
- New code comments or tests: test files, test scripts or CI test steps.
- A rule in `AGENTS.md` broken.
- Docs that now lie: `AGENTS.md`, the README or a skill that no longer matches
  the code.

## Taste calls

Layout, spacing, typography, responsive behavior, motion, image crops, and any
"close enough to the design" call need a designer's eye. Don't approve or
reject them on your own. Check the screenshots exist, then flag:
"**Designer's eye**: <the call>".

## Don't flag

- Formatting and lint style. The linter already enforces it.
- Naming or structure preferences with no bug behind them.
- Generated files (only check they were regenerated), lockfiles, build output,
  or binary assets.
- Nits that would cost an agent author a whole new commit and review round.
  Leave them out.

## How to report

- Every finding gets a tag: **Important** (must fix before merge), **Nit**
  (optional, only if cheap), or **Pre-existing** (was already there, don't
  block the PR on it).
- Every finding gets a real `file:line`. Never guess a filename.
- Name the class of problem, so the author fixes every instance in one go.
- Start with a one-line summary: how many findings by tag, or a clear "No
  issues found."

## When to stop

- Round one reviews the full diff. Every round after that reviews only what
  changed since the last one.
- Never repeat a finding that was already raised or closed with a reason.
- Stop at the lane's cap: fast 1, standard 2, deep 3. At the cap, don't ask
  for another fix. Ask the author to rethink the approach, or hand it to a
  person.
- Your approval never replaces a required human one.

# Controlling Ketch's UI

Ketch ships its own banner, modal, preferences center and floating button. This
file documents the surface it exposes so a project can keep, restyle, reposition
or replace any of it. **None of these choices is "the" right one** — pick per
project and per design.

## What Ketch actually renders

All of it is **light DOM — there is no shadow root**, so ordinary CSS reaches it.

| Element | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `<div id="lanyard_root">` | Host for every experience: banner, modal, preferences, consent gate |
| `<div id="lanyard_fab_button">` | The floating button. Inserted as **`body.firstChild`** |
| `#ketch-banner` | The banner container |
| `#ketch-banner-content` | Banner copy area |
| `#ketch-banner-buttons-container-standard` / `-compact` | Banner button rows (which one depends on the configured size) |
| `#ketch-banner-button-*` | Individual banner buttons |
| `#ketch-modal` | The "customize settings" modal |
| `#ketch-preferences` | The preferences center |
| `#ketch-preferences-purposes-tab`, `-subscriptions-tab`, `-requests-tab`, … | Preference center tabs |

At runtime Ketch also appends a `<style>` to `<head>` containing
`:root { --k-…: …; }` with its whole resolved theme. **That stylesheet lands
after the project's CSS** — the single most important fact for overriding it.

The floating button is only rendered when both are true:

- the property config has an `accessibilityButton` object, and
- experiences aren't disabled.

So removing `accessibilityButton` in the Ketch dashboard is the only way to stop
it being created at all. Everything below is client-side.

## Choice 1 — the floating button

### Keep it (Ketch's default)

Do nothing. Position and colour come from `accessibilityButton` in the
dashboard (`position: "bottom-left" | "bottom-right" | …`, `color`). Change it
there, no code.

### Reposition or restyle it

```css
#lanyard_fab_button {
  inset: auto 1.5rem 1.5rem auto;
  z-index: 40;
}
```

Useful when the dashboard's corner collides with a chat widget or a sticky CTA.

### Hide it

```css
#lanyard_fab_button {
  display: none !important;
}
```

`!important` is **required**: Ketch toggles this element's inline
`style.display` when experiences open and close, and an inline style beats any
plain rule. Without it the button reappears after the banner is dismissed.

If the project's linter forbids `!important`, scope an override rather than
dropping it — the rule doesn't work without it:

```jsonc
// biome.json → overrides
{
  "includes": ["lib/integrations/ketch/ketch-experience.css"],
  "linter": { "rules": { "complexity": { "noImportantStyles": "off" } } }
}
```

Hiding it in CSS is a patch: Ketch still mounts the element on every page.
Removing `accessibilityButton` from the dashboard is the durable fix. Do both
when you have dashboard access; flag it as a follow-up when you don't.

## Choice 2 — where preferences are reachable from

Consent has to stay reopenable after the banner is gone. Any of these works:

| Option | How |
| --- | --- |
| Ketch's floating button | Default, nothing to build |
| A footer link | Render a button that calls `openPreferences()` |
| A nav / settings menu item | Same call, different mount point |
| A privacy-policy page link | Same call |
| Several at once | Fine — the call is idempotent |

The integration's `openPreferences()` helper opens the preferences center as a
**modal** over the current page, not a full-page navigation:

```ts
window.ketch("showConsent", { displayHint: "experiences.consent.modal" })
```

Prefer routing it through the integration's helper (`openPreferences()` from
`useConsent()`) so nothing else touches `window.ketch`.

It is safe to call before the SDK has loaded — it queues on `window.semaphore`
and dispatches after init — so a control doesn't need to wait for readiness or
be disabled on first paint.

Related commands:

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `ketch("showConsent", { displayHint: "experiences.consent.modal" })` | Open preferences as a modal — what `openPreferences()` calls |
| `ketch("showPreferences")` | Open the full-page preference experience instead of a modal |
| `ketch("showConsent")` | Re-show the consent banner |
| `ketch("showPreferences", { tab: "purposes" })` | Open the full-page experience on a specific tab |

Whichever mount point you choose, put it somewhere **every template renders** —
usually the footer or a persistent nav — and verify it on a route that isn't the
homepage.

## Choice 3 — styling

Three approaches. They compose; pick by how much design control the project
needs and whether you have dashboard access.

### A. Theme it in the Ketch dashboard

Set colours, radii and fonts in the property's theme editor.

- **For:** survives any code change, no CSS to maintain, works for teams
  without frontend access.
- **Against:** hex values duplicated from the design system, so it drifts when
  tokens change; needs dashboard access; can't reference CSS variables.

Best when the site's palette is stable and nobody wants Ketch CSS in the repo.

### B. Override the `--k-*` variables (token-driven)

Ketch's components consume their theme through CSS custom properties, so
redefining them restyles the UI without touching structure:

```css
html:root {
  --k-banner-container-background-color: var(--color-primary);
  --k-banner-header-title-color: var(--color-secondary);
  --k-banner-description-link-color: var(--color-contrast);
  --k-banner-buttons-primary-background-color: var(--color-secondary);
  --k-banner-buttons-primary-text-color: var(--color-primary);
}
```

- **For:** the design system stays the single source of truth — when tokens
  change, Ketch follows automatically, no edits.
- **Against:** variable names are Ketch-internal and could change across SDK
  versions; only covers what the theme models.

**Use `html:root`, not `:root`.** Ketch injects its own `:root` block into
`<head>` at runtime, so it comes after the project stylesheet and wins on equal
specificity. `html:root` is one step higher and wins regardless of order.
`:root { … !important }` also works; `html:root` is cleaner.

#### Deriving the variable names

The rule is mechanical: **take the theme value's dot path and replace dots with
dashes, prefixed `--k-`.**

```
banner.container.background.color   →  --k-banner-container-background-color
modal.purposeList.switchButtons.on.background.color
                                    →  --k-modal-purposeList-switchButtons-on-background-color
```

Casing is preserved, so `purposeList` stays camelCase. Enumerate what's
available for the property:

```bash
curl -s https://global.ketchcdn.com/web/v3/config/<org>/<property>/production/default/en/config.json \
  | jq '.theme.banner, .theme.modal, .theme.preference'
```

Watch out for non-colour values. Radii are sometimes stored unitless (`"8"`),
which is invalid in `border-radius: var(…)` — set those explicitly with a unit
(`8px`) or handle them with direct CSS instead.

### C. Direct CSS on the element IDs

For anything the theme doesn't model — layout, stacking, spacing, responsive
behaviour, fonts:

```css
#lanyard_root,
#lanyard_root * {
  font-family: var(--font-sans), system-ui, sans-serif !important;
}

@media (max-width: 640px) {
  #ketch-banner {
    inset-inline: 0 !important;
    width: 100% !important;
    border-radius: 0 !important;
    padding-bottom: max(1rem, var(--safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)) !important;
  }

  #ketch-banner-buttons-container-standard {
    flex-direction: column !important;
    width: 100% !important;
  }
}
```

`!important` is usually needed here because Ketch's internals are Tailwind
classes with an `!` important prefix reading the variables (e.g.
`!ketch-bg-[--k-banner-container-background-color]`).

Ketch exposes safe-area values on its root for notched devices:
`--safe-area-inset-top` / `-right` / `-bottom` / `-left`.

- **For:** total control, reaches everything.
- **Against:** couples to Ketch's DOM, so it's the first thing to break on an
  SDK upgrade. Prefer B for colours and keep C for structure.

### D. Replace the UI entirely

Possible — suppress Ketch's experiences and drive consent with `setConsent` from
a custom component. **Think hard before doing this.** You take on per-jurisdiction
copy, GPC and ATT signal banners, vendor lists, TCF strings and the audit trail,
which is the bulk of what the CMP is paid for. Only justified when design
requirements genuinely cannot be met by A–C, and worth confirming with whoever
owns compliance.

## Verifying UI changes

CSS against a third-party widget can't be verified from a build — check in a
browser:

1. Clear site data so the banner shows again (or use `ketch("showConsent")`).
2. Banner: colours, fonts, button styles, and the link to the privacy policy.
3. Open "customize settings": purpose toggles, accept/reject buttons, scrolling.
4. Dismiss the banner and confirm the floating button is in the state you
   intended — this is where a missing `!important` shows up.
5. Mobile viewport, and a notched device if safe-area padding matters.
6. Keyboard: tab through the banner and modal, confirm focus is visible and
   trapped in the modal.

## Testing a different jurisdiction

The banner and preferences center render completely differently per
jurisdiction, so "the toggles are locked" or "Accept All does nothing" is
usually **not a bug** — it's the visitor resolving to a jurisdiction where every
purpose is `disclosure` (notice-only). Ketch then shows each purpose as
**"Always Active"** with the toggle disabled, and the accept/reject buttons have
nothing to change. Check the legal basis before debugging the UI:

```bash
curl -s https://global.ketchcdn.com/web/v3/config/<org>/<property>/production/default/en/config.json \
  | jq -r '.purposes[] | "\(.code) \(.legalBasisCode)"'
```

Force a jurisdiction instead of relying on geo-IP by setting an attribute on the
root element:

```html
<html jurisdiction="gdpr">
```

For a quick manual check with no code change, Ketch also accepts a URL query
parameter that sets the same thing:

```
https://example.com/?ketch_jurisdiction=gdpr
```

Verified against a real property: LatAm traffic normally resolves to
`default` (notice-only), where consent is granted automatically and the
banner won't re-show on reload — see the gotcha below.
`?ketch_jurisdiction=gdpr` (or `US_Texas`, `US_California`, …) forces the
banner to render for that jurisdiction instead, with real Accept/Reject
buttons — no VPN needed. Use this to actually see the opt-in UI from a
region that defaults to notice-only.

In Next.js, drive it from a gitignored env var so it never ships:

```tsx
<html
  lang="en"
  {...(forcedJurisdiction
    ? ({ jurisdiction: forcedJurisdiction } as Record<string, string>)
    : {})}
>
```

Ketch's resolution order, highest priority first:

1. An override in Ketch's own storage
2. `config.jurisdiction.code`
3. **`document.documentElement.getAttribute("jurisdiction")`**
4. A `dataLayer` variable, if the property configures one
5. The region → jurisdiction map (`jurisdiction.scopes` in `boot.js`)
6. `defaultJurisdictionCode`

Because the attribute is checked before the region map, it works from anywhere
with no VPN. Try `gdpr` or `US_California` for opt-in UI with live toggles,
`US_Texas` for opt-out, `default` for notice-only.

Countries absent from `jurisdiction.scopes` fall through to `default`. If the
site has real traffic from a country that isn't mapped, that's a dashboard
decision for whoever owns compliance — surface it rather than working around it.

## Gotchas

- **Opt-out and notice-only jurisdictions don't offer Reject, and the banner
  won't re-show.** Once Ketch auto-grants a jurisdiction's default record,
  that resolves `isResolved` the same way an explicit accept would — no
  reload brings the banner back, and there's no Reject All to click if you
  were expecting one. This is the jurisdiction's legal basis, not a bug in
  the integration or a broken build. Force a different jurisdiction (above)
  before assuming something's wrong.
- **`options.appDivs`.** The property config can list element IDs that Ketch
  gates on consent (commonly a chat widget container). If a third-party widget
  mysteriously doesn't appear, check whether it's listed there.
- **Ketch normalises margins/padding** inside `#lanyard_root` with its own
  injected stylesheet. Reset-style rules of your own may be redundant or fight
  it.
- **Ketch's stylesheet is added on first experience render**, not at boot. A
  rule that works on the banner may not have applied yet when you inspect
  before it opens.
- **Custom CSS in the dashboard.** The property supports a `customCss` field
  injected at runtime. If overrides behave unpredictably, check whether
  something is already set there before adding more CSS in the repo.

# Accessibility

Contrast, motion and target size are design decisions. Report failures; don't
change brand colors or layout unasked.

## A11Y-01 · Every page has an `h1`

**Fix before launch**

One `h1` that names the page. Screen reader users jump to it first.

**Check:** `curl -s localhost:3000/<route> | grep -c '<h1'` prints at least `1`.

## A11Y-02 · Everything works by keyboard

**Fix before launch**

Interactive elements are real controls (`<button>`, `<Link>`, inputs), reachable
with Tab, with a visible focus style. A `<div onClick>` can't be reached
without a mouse. Menus and modals close on Escape and return focus.

**Check (browser):** Tab through the page. Every control is reachable, and
you can always see where focus is.

## A11Y-03 · Icon-only controls have a name

**Fix before launch**

An icon-only button or link carries an `aria-label` or visually hidden text.
Otherwise a screen reader announces only "button".

## A11Y-04 · Inputs have labels

**Fix before launch**

Each input has a `<label>`. A placeholder isn't one; it disappears as soon as
someone types. Fields for personal data carry the matching `autocomplete`
value (`email`, `name`, `tel`).

## A11Y-05 · Text meets contrast

**Fix before launch**

Body text is at least 4.5:1 against its background, and large text (24px, or
19px bold) at least 3:1. Logos, disabled controls and decorative text are
exempt.

**Check (browser):** Lighthouse's accessibility audit, or the axe DevTools
extension.

## A11Y-06 · Motion can be paused or reduced

**Fix before launch**

Anything that moves on its own for more than 5 seconds (autoplay video,
marquees, carousels) has a pause control. Non-essential animation, smooth
scrolling included, respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## A11Y-07 · Targets are big enough; zoom stays on

**Fix before launch**

Tap targets are at least 24×24px, or have 24px of clearance. Links inside a
sentence are exempt.

Never set `maximumScale: 1` or `userScalable: false` in the viewport. If iOS
zooms into a focused input, set the input's font size to at least 16px instead.

## A11Y-08 · No horizontal scroll at 320px

**Fix before launch**

The page fits a 320px-wide viewport without horizontal scrolling. Maps, data
tables and diagrams are exempt.

# Content

## CONTENT-01 · Indexed copy is in the server HTML

**Must not ship** · only if indexed

Text meant for search, link previews and AI is in the server HTML. Don't draw
it only in a canvas, and don't load it only through `dynamic(..., { ssr: false })`.
A WebGL scene can stay client-only; its headline and copy can't.

**Check:** a sentence from the page's main copy appears in
`curl -s localhost:3000/<route>`.

## CONTENT-02 · No placeholder output

**Must not ship**

No `undefined`, `null`, `NaN`, `[object Object]` or lorem ipsum in rendered
text. These usually appear after launch, when an editor leaves a CMS field
empty, so render nothing for a missing field instead.

**Check:**

```bash
curl -s localhost:3000/<route> | grep -noiE 'undefined|NaN|\[object Object\]|lorem ipsum'
```

A match is a lead, not proof: documentation can say "returns `undefined`" on
purpose.

## CONTENT-03 · Each fact has one source

**Must not ship**

A price, spec or limit shown in more than one place reads from one module or
one CMS field. Two copies drift, and the site contradicts itself.

**Check:** search the repo for the value. It appears once, where it's defined.

## CONTENT-04 · No test pages, drafts or staging links

**Must not ship**

Test pages, unpublished drafts and links to staging or preview hosts aren't
reachable in production or listed in the sitemap.

**Check:** search the production HTML and `sitemap.xml` for `test`, `staging`,
`preview` and `vercel.app`.

## CONTENT-05 · No starter leftovers

**Fix before launch**

Replace basement's placeholders with the site's own, wherever they remain:

- the `app/favicon.ico` every template ships
- the `"Basement Starter"` title in `app/layout.tsx`
- `siteName = "Basement"` in `lib/utils/metadata.ts`
- the `"Basement Next Starter"` homepage heading

**Check:**

```bash
grep -rn 'Basement Starter\|Basement Next Starter\|siteName = "Basement"' app lib components
```

# Crawlers

## CRAWL-01 · Indexing matches the decision

**Must not ship** when production and the decision disagree

`app/robots.ts` and each page's `noIndex` follow *Indexed by search engines*.
Previews are never indexable.

The starter indexes only the host of `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, and on Vercel
only on a production deployment. Every other host, including `*.vercel.app`,
gets `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` and a disallow-all `robots.txt`. Without
`NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, nothing is indexed.

**Check:**

```bash
curl -s https://<production>/robots.txt
curl -sI https://<production>/ | grep -i x-robots-tag
curl -sI https://<preview>/ | grep -i x-robots-tag
```

Production matches the decision. The preview prints `noindex`.

## CRAWL-02 · Canonicals point at the right page

**Must not ship**

A canonical is absolute and points at a page that returns 200 and is indexable.

If `app/layout.tsx` sets `alternates.canonical: "/"`, every page that doesn't
set its own canonical inherits it, which points the whole site at the
homepage. Set it per page with `generatePageMetadata({ url })`, or remove it
from the layout.

If the layout declares an `en-US` alternate at `/en-US`, remove it unless a
route serves that locale.

**Check:**

```bash
curl -s localhost:3000/<route> | grep -o '<link rel="canonical"[^>]*>'
```

It names that route, not `/`.

## CRAWL-03 · The sitemap lists every indexable page

**Fix before launch** · only if indexed

Build the sitemap from the same data as the routes: every static route, plus
each CMS document with a public URL. The starter's `app/sitemap.xml/route.ts`
lists only `/`; add each route to `getStaticEntries()`. When the sitemap reads
a CMS, a new content type needs adding to its query.

**Check:**

```bash
curl -s localhost:3000/sitemap.xml | grep -c '<loc>'
```

The count matches the number of public pages.

## CRAWL-04 · The sitemap lists only live pages

**Fix before launch** · only if indexed

No sitemap URL redirects, 404s or is `noindex`, and each one uses the
production host.

**Check:**

```bash
curl -s localhost:3000/sitemap.xml | grep -o '<loc>[^<]*' | cut -c6- |
  while read -r u; do printf '%s %s\n' "$(curl -so /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$u")" "$u"; done
```

Every line starts with `200`.

## CRAWL-05 · AI crawler policy matches the decision

**Fix before launch**

- *AI crawlers: allowed* needs nothing.
- *AI crawlers: blocked* adds a `disallow: "/"` rule in `robots.ts` for each
  agent: `GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `PerplexityBot`, `Google-Extended`, `CCBot`.
- *llms.txt: yes* serves `/llms.txt`.

**Check:** `curl -s https://<production>/robots.txt` matches the decision.

# On the real domain

These only fail in production, so check them against the deployed URL.

## LAUNCH-01 · Forms deliver on production

**Must not ship** · only if the site has forms

Submit each form on production and confirm the submission arrives. The usual
failure: the form's API key is set for Preview but not for Production, so the
form works on every preview and silently drops submissions after launch.

## LAUNCH-02 · CMS publishing updates production

**Must not ship** · only if the site uses a CMS

Publish a small change in the CMS and confirm production shows it. The
revalidation webhook points at the production URL and carries its secret.

## LAUNCH-03 · One host

**Fix before launch**

Pick the apex domain or `www`. In Vercel's domain settings, the other
redirects to it permanently.

**Check:**

```bash
curl -sI https://<other-host>/ | grep -i '^location'
```

It points at the chosen host.

## LAUNCH-04 · Old URLs redirect on a relaunch

**Fix before launch** · only if *Replaces an existing site: yes*

Every old URL with traffic or backlinks redirects to its new equivalent
through `redirects()` in `next.config.ts`. Ask the user for the old site's URL
list: its sitemap, or its top pages in analytics.

**Check:** request a sample of old URLs. Each returns `308` to a page that
returns `200`.

# Metadata

## META-01 · Every page has a real title

**Must not ship**

Each route exports `metadata` or `generateMetadata` with its own title. If
`app/layout.tsx` still has the `"Basement Starter"` default and its
`"%s - Basement Starter"` template, replace both with the site's name.

**Check:**

```bash
curl -s localhost:3000/<route> | grep -o '<title>[^<]*'
```

## META-02 · Metadata is in the server HTML

**Must not ship**

Set titles, descriptions and share tags through the Metadata API, never with
`document.title` or a client effect. Crawlers and link previews don't run
JavaScript.

**Check:** the tags appear in `curl -s localhost:3000/<route>`, not only in
the browser's DOM.

## META-03 · The share image loads

**Must not ship**

A declared `og:image` is absolute and returns an image.

If the layout or `generatePageMetadata` defaults to `/opengraph-image.jpg`,
add that file: no template ships it. Until `public/opengraph-image.jpg`
exists, every share card is broken, and so is the Organization JSON-LD logo,
which uses the same path.

**Check:**

```bash
img=$(curl -s localhost:3000/ | grep -o 'property="og:image" content="[^"]*' | cut -d'"' -f4)
curl -so /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}\n' "$img"
```

Expect `200 image/...`.

## META-04 · No `localhost` URLs in production

**Must not ship**

`metadataBase`, canonicals and share URLs read `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, then
the Vercel deployment URL, and fall back to `http://localhost:3000` off Vercel.
Set it for the Production environment.

**Check:**

```bash
curl -s https://<production>/ | grep -c 'localhost:3000'
```

Expect `0`.

## META-05 · Titles are unique

**Fix before launch**

Distinct pages have distinct titles. Variants that canonicalize to one page
are exempt.

## META-06 · Public pages have a description

**Fix before launch**

Slack, LinkedIn and iMessage show the description as the preview text. If the
layout's default reads `package.json`'s `description`, write a real one there.

## META-07 · `<html lang>` matches the content

**Fix before launch**

The starter sets `lang="en"`. Change it when the site isn't English, and set
it per locale on a multilingual site.

# Performance

## PERF-01 · The LCP image isn't lazy

**Fix before launch**

The largest image in the first screen (usually the hero) passes `priority` to
`@/components/ui/image`. Everything below the fold stays lazy, which is the
default.

## PERF-02 · Image `sizes` match the layout

**Fix before launch**

`sizes` describes the width the image renders at. Without it, the image
component falls back to `100vw` and the browser downloads the largest
variant, which is only right for full-width images. Build `sizes` with
`buildImageSizes` or `buildGridImageSizes` from `lib/utils/image-sizes.ts`.

The `no-fill-without-sizes` lint rule catches `fill` with no `sizes`. It can't
tell whether the value is correct.

## PERF-03 · Responses are compressed

**Fix before launch** · only when hosted outside Vercel

Vercel compresses responses by default. Another host has to serve HTML, JS
and CSS with gzip or brotli.

**Check:**

```bash
curl -sI -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip, br' https://<production>/ | grep -i content-encoding
```

Expect `gzip` or `br`.

# Routing

## ROUTE-01 · Missing pages return 404

**Must not ship**

When a dynamic or CMS route has no data, call `notFound()` before any
`<Suspense>`. Once a response starts streaming, its status is already 200.
Next can't change it then, and injects a `noindex` tag instead.

```tsx
export default async function Page({ params }: PageProps<"/blog/[slug]">) {
  const { slug } = await params
  const post = await getPost(slug)
  if (!post) notFound()
  return <Post post={post} />
}
```

**Check:**

```bash
curl -so /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' localhost:3000/does-not-exist
```

Expect `404`. Repeat under each dynamic segment, such as `/blog/does-not-exist`.

**Not this:** redirecting unknown paths to `/`. That's still a missing page
answering 200.

## ROUTE-02 · No internal link is broken

**Must not ship**

Every internal link resolves to a page that returns 200. A control that only
runs JavaScript is a `<button>`, not `<a href="#">`. An `#id` that exists on the
page, or a "back to top" link, is fine.

**Check:** list each route's links and request them.

```bash
curl -s localhost:3000/ | grep -o 'href="/[^"#]*"' | cut -d'"' -f2 | sort -u |
  while read -r p; do printf '%s %s\n' "$(curl -so /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "localhost:3000$p")" "$p"; done
```

Every line starts with `200`. A broken link in the nav or footer breaks on every
page, so check those first.

# Security and hygiene

## SEC-01 · `NEXT_PUBLIC_` holds only public keys

**Must not ship**

Anything prefixed `NEXT_PUBLIC_` ships in the browser bundle, readable by
anyone. Only keys designed to be public belong there: a Sanity project ID, a
Stripe `pk_` key, an analytics site ID. Read every other secret on the server.

**Check:**

```bash
grep -rhoE 'NEXT_PUBLIC_[A-Z0-9_]+' app components lib | sort -u
```

Confirm each name on the list is meant to be public.

## SEC-02 · Tracking matches the consent decision

**Fix before launch** · only if consent is required

No analytics or ad script runs, and no tracking cookie is set, before the
visitor answers the consent banner. The `ketch-consent-check` skill covers
gating a script behind Ketch, when the project has it.

**Check (browser):** in a fresh private window, before you answer the banner,
DevTools → Application → Cookies lists no tracking cookies.

## SEC-03 · No first-party console errors

**Fix before launch**

The console shows no errors from the site's own code on load, and no
hydration mismatches. A mismatch means the server and the client rendered
different content. Errors from third-party scripts are out of scope.

**Check (browser):** load each route with DevTools open, then read the
console.

# Fast-lane merge

The `fast` label is the final session-review sign-off. Add it **only after
every required review has finished cleanly**, including an independent,
fresh-context agent review using `REVIEW.md`. The workflow does not run
another AI reviewer.

The fast lane is an extra path for the changes under "What can merge". It needs no human
approval and changes nothing about how every other PR is reviewed and merged.

## Install and activate

New projects get these files during scaffolding. In an existing repo, run:

```sh
bunx bsmnt install review --repo
```

Later, `bunx bsmnt update review` refreshes the kit to the latest release —
the skills on your machine and, in a repo that has it, these files — and
keeps `.github/fast-lane.json` as it is.

1. Review and merge the installation PR into the default branch. The workflow
   and allowlist always load from there, never from the PR being merged.
2. Require the repo's actual CI checks in GitHub branch protection or rulesets.
   Without registered required checks, the workflow refuses to merge.
   `--protect` suggests the checks that ran on the last merged PR, warns about
   any name that never ran, and preserves existing rules.
3. Create the GitHub label `fast` if it does not exist:

   ```sh
   gh label create fast --description "Final clean session review; eligible for automatic merge"
   ```

4. Point the allowlist at internal Markdown this repo actually has. The
   default `docs/internal/` often doesn't exist, so that docs-only route is
   unavailable; the default `.github/fast-lane.json` also turns on the risk
   gate, which can merge other eligible changes (see "What can merge").
   Check paths are genuinely internal, not published site copy. The installer
   reports the risk gate and warns when no allowlisted paths exist and no risk
   gate is configured. Edit the config through a human-reviewed PR.
5. Pilot with a small internal note. Complete all reviews, then add `fast`.

The kit is the standard: the installer overwrites this guide, the workflow,
the script, `REVIEW.md`, the PR template and the `AGENTS.md` block, and lists
what it overwrote. `.github/fast-lane.json` is per-repo config and is kept
once it exists. GitHub's required-approvals setting can't vary by label, so if
the repo's branch rules require approvals, GitHub still applies them to Fast
PRs; the fast lane itself adds no approval step.

## Daily use

- Finish the solution, checks and every required review in the working session.
  The independent reviewer can run before or after opening the PR, but must
  review the final commit. Record the reviewed SHA and result in the PR.
- Resolve all findings and required threads. Respect the lane's round cap.
  Fast has one round; blocking findings escalate instead of looping.
- Only an operator with write access, or their session agent using that
  credential, adds `fast` as the last review step:

  ```sh
  gh pr edit <number> --add-label fast
  ```

- The workflow checks the real diff and waits up to 15 minutes for required CI.
  It then squash-merges that exact SHA, subject to GitHub branch rules.
  It never enables GitHub's queued auto-merge, so a later push cannot inherit
  an already queued merge.
- New commits, PR edits, reopening or conversion to draft invalidate `fast`.
  Removing it also stops a waiting run. Finish the required reviews again
  before reapplying it; a new commit does not reset the review-round cap.
- Missing, failed or timed-out checks leave the PR open. Read the workflow
  result; after fixing the cause and finishing any needed review, remove and
  reapply `fast`. No background retry loop runs.
- PRs without `fast` are never merged by this workflow, even with green CI.

The label is a trusted attestation, not independent proof that a reviewer ran.
CI can verify the diff, permissions and checks, not the operator's judgment.

## What can merge

Every route: only added or modified text files, so no deletions, renames,
binaries, symlinks or executables; a complete diff and tree; and no fork,
draft, closed or non-default-branch PRs.

**Allowlisted Markdown.** Ordinary `.md` files in `allowedPaths`, which takes
exact `.md` paths or directory prefixes ending in `/`, not globs. No size cap.
Policy files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `REVIEW.md`, `SKILL.md`) and
dot-directories never count as allowlisted.

**Risk gate.** At most `maxChangedLines` (200 or fewer) added and deleted
lines, not counting lockfiles or the generated Sanity files
(`lib/integrations/sanity/sanity.types.ts` and `schema.json`, optionally under
`src/`), so a dependency or schema change follows the score
instead of the size cap. With `"riskGate": { "maxScore": 49 }` in `.github/fast-lane.json`,
any other change can merge when the PR body's Risk block (from the `pr-risk`
skill) has exactly one of each line:

- `**Score**: N/100`, with N at most `maxScore` (never above 49)
- `**Lane**: fast`, optionally followed by `· **Review rounds**: N`
- `**Designer's eye**: not needed`, optionally followed by `— ` and a
  reason that never asks for a reviewer
- `**Human review**: not required by the lane`, optional, but a line that
  asks for a person stops the merge

The workflow trusts those lines the way it trusts the label: as the
operator's signed-off assessment. The reviewer checks them against the diff.
Editing the PR body removes `fast`, so a sign-off can't outlive the block it
read. Template hints, code spans (including spans that wrap lines), fenced and
indented code, and link-reference
definitions are ignored. Delete `riskGate` to go back to Markdown only.

**Visual changes with proof.** When the diff touches components, images,
stylesheets, shaders or rendered content (`.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.vue`, `.svelte`,
`.astro`, `.mdx`, `.html`, `.svg`, `.css`, `.scss`, `.sass`, `.less`, `.styl`, `.glsl`), the PR body must
attach visual proof — mobile and
desktop screenshots, the `visual-proof` skill — and the eye line's reason must
be exactly one of the no-taste-call phrases:

- `implements the design file exactly`
- `token-only values from the existing scales`
- `refactor with identical rendering`
- `visual nit on an existing component`
- `no visual change`

A diff that adds a component file (`.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.vue`, `.svelte`,
`.astro`) never merges here: building a component needs a designer, whatever
the eye line says. That includes a component split into a new file.

The proof is at least two attachments, with one labelled mobile (375) and one
desktop (1440): the `visual-proof` table's columns, a caption line above each
shot, or the width in the filename. A single screenshot is not proof. What the
shots show stays with the reviewer; the workflow only checks that both
viewports are attached.

Plain `.md` files are documentation, not rendered content: they take the
allowlist route or the risk gate, and screenshots would say nothing about them.
A repo that renders Markdown as page copy should turn the risk gate off.

Any other reason is a taste call: it stays with a designer. The
workflow creates and adds the `designer-audit` label to every PR it fast-merges
with a visual diff, so the designer can review the merged batch weekly and
revert anything wrong.

Some paths always need a person, whatever the Risk block says: dot-directories
(`.github/`, `.env*`, `.agents/`), agent and review instructions, `CODEOWNERS`,
Renovate, build/test/CI/deployment/tool configuration and
`scripts/bsmnt-fast-lane.mjs`. Auth and secrets, and CI or review-policy files,
stay human through the Risk block. Dependencies and lockfiles, brand, design
tokens and UI copy follow the score, so a small one can merge here. Taste calls
never do: the eye line has to name one of the no-taste-call reasons.

# Review guidelines

For anyone reviewing a PR, agent or person, whatever tool runs the review.
Read it with the repo's `AGENTS.md`.

Find the bugs that would hurt users or mislead the next person. Skip the
rest. A review that flags ten nits and misses one stale-cache bug failed.

## Before you start

- Read the PR body. It must have **Summary**, **Testing**, **Risk** and **How
  to revert**. If one is missing or empty, that is your first finding.
- Use the `## Risk` block's lane for your depth and round limit. If the score
  looks wrong for the diff, say so and why.
- A fast-lane PR can merge on its Risk block's **Score**, **Lane** and
  **Designer's eye** lines. Check each against the diff. A forced category or a
  score that should be 50 or more means the PR is not fast: flag it as
  **Important**. A visual change still needs mobile and desktop screenshots,
  and a taste call still needs a designer. Visual nits on an existing
  component and schema changes on an existing type are fast when the score
  allows; building a component never is.
- Check the proof, not the claim. "Tested locally" with no output is level 1
  evidence. A visual change without mobile and desktop screenshots is not
  ready.

## What counts as a failure

Flag these as **Important**:

- The change doesn't do what the PR says, or a bug fix patches the symptom
  instead of the root cause.
- It breaks something else: a caller, another consumer of the same data, a
  layout or style shared across pages.
- Stale data: caching or invalidation no longer covers what changed.
- Generated files (types, clients, schemas) left out of date in the same PR.
- A secret in plaintext, or an auth or permission check weakened.
- A broken user path: a dead link, a missing redirect, a page that renders
  empty, metadata or the sitemap dropping a page.
- Debug code or UI that ships to production.
- New code comments or tests: test files, test scripts or CI test steps.
- A rule in `AGENTS.md` broken.
- Docs that now lie: `AGENTS.md`, the README or a skill that no longer matches
  the code.

## Taste calls

Layout, spacing, typography, responsive behavior, motion, image crops, and any
"close enough to the design" call need a designer's eye. Don't approve or
reject them on your own. Check the screenshots exist, then flag:
"**Designer's eye**: <the call>".

A visual nit on an existing component (a small fix to alignment, spacing,
sizing, colour, corners, hover or a breakpoint) is not a taste call; the
designer audits it after merge. Building a component is: a new component,
block, section or page, or new UI an existing component didn't render before.
A PR that builds one and claims the nit reason is **Important**.

## Don't flag

- Formatting and lint style. The linter already enforces it.
- Naming or structure preferences with no bug behind them.
- Generated files (only check they were regenerated), lockfiles, build output,
  or binary assets.
- Nits that would cost an agent author a whole new commit and review round.
  Leave them out.

## How to report

- Every finding gets a tag: **Important** (must fix before merge), **Nit**
  (optional, only if cheap), or **Pre-existing** (was already there, don't
  block the PR on it).
- Every finding gets a real `file:line`. Never guess a filename.
- Name the class of problem, so the author fixes every instance in one go.
- Start with a one-line summary: how many findings by tag, or a clear "No
  issues found."

## When to stop

- Round one reviews the full diff. Every round after that reviews only what
  changed since the last one.
- Never repeat a finding that was already raised or closed with a reason.
- Stop at the lane's cap: fast 1, standard 2, deep 3. At the cap, don't ask
  for another fix. Ask the author to rethink the approach, or hand it to a
  person.
- Your approval never replaces a required human one.

## Next.js + Sanity page builder

Applies when the repo is a Next.js + Sanity page builder (it has a
`sanity.config.ts` and `components/page-builder/`). Also flag as
**Important**:

- A one-off page hand-written under `app/`. Pages live in Sanity. A
  collection (a blog, for example) gets its own document type and route, and
  tooling routes like `/studio` and `/components` are fine.
- A block missing its registry entry or fixture, or a block root that renders
  its own `<section>` or vertical padding.
- Hardcoded px for section spacing instead of the spacing scale.
- A schema or query change without regenerated `sanity.types.ts` in the same
  PR, or a new `gatedContent` field missing from its explicit GROQ branch.
- A bare Sanity client instead of `sanityFetch` / `fetchSanity`, or a new
  layout singleton missing from `SANITY_LAYOUT_TAGS`. Both serve stale content.
- `headers()`, `cookies()`, `draftMode()` or `searchParams` in a root layout.
- `useMemo`, `useCallback`, `React.memo` or `forwardRef` (React Compiler is on).
- Debug UI that can reach production with no gate in front of it.

Don't flag anything inside `sanity.types.ts`. Only check it was regenerated.

Where a change also shows up: the sitemap, the RSS feed, JSON-LD and the
`/components` preview all read the same projections. A spread `...`
projection returns new fields to every consumer. Nav, footer and the spacing
scale touch every page.

Previewing a block: `/components?component=<blockType>` only renders inside
the Studio, so it 404s when opened directly. Open `/studio` first, then
navigate from that page (for example run
`location.href = "/components?component=featuresGrid"`).

# Markdown Proxy — Adding New Content Types

This project serves Sanity content as markdown for AI agents. Each content type (article, etc.) has a dedicated route handler that fetches from Sanity and returns formatted markdown.

## Architecture Overview

```
Request: GET /blog/my-post.md
    |
proxy.ts — rewrites to /api/blog/my-post.md
    |
app/api/blog/[slug]/route.ts — validates .md extension, strips it, fetches from Sanity, returns markdown
```

Route handlers live under `/api/` so `page.tsx` can coexist at the public path (e.g. `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` for the HTML page). The `proxy.ts` file rewrites `.md` URLs to the API routes transparently.

**Key files:**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `app/api/{type}/[slug]/route.ts` | API route handler per content type (serves markdown) |
| `app/sitemap.md/route.ts` | Discovery endpoint listing all markdown content |
| `proxy.ts` | Rewrites `.md` URLs to API routes, handles `Accept: text/markdown` |
| `lib/integrations/sanity/markdown-proxy.config.ts` | Route config for proxy rewrites |
| `lib/integrations/sanity/utils/link.ts` | `CONTENT_TYPE_TO_PATH` mapping for internal link resolution |
| `lib/integrations/sanity/queries.ts` | GROQ queries for each content type |
| `lib/utils/portable-text-to-markdown.ts` | Shared Portable Text to markdown converter |
| `lib/integrations/sanity/live/index.tsx` | `SanityFetch` helper for markdown routes |

**Access patterns:**

1. **Direct URL**: `GET /blog/my-post.md` — proxy rewrites to `/api/blog/my-post.md`, route handler validates `.md`, strips it, serves markdown
2. **Accept header**: `GET /blog/my-post` with `Accept: text/markdown` — proxy rewrites to `/api/blog/my-post.md`
3. **Without `.md`**: `GET /blog/my-post` — serves the HTML page (if `page.tsx` exists), not markdown
4. **Discovery**: `GET /sitemap.md` — lists all available markdown content

## Step-by-Step: Add a New Content Type

Example: adding a `blog` content type backed by Sanity document type `blog`.

### 1. Check your Sanity schema

Look at your schema definition in `lib/integrations/sanity/schemas/` to understand the fields. Every field you want in the markdown output needs to be queried and rendered.

### 2. Add a GROQ query

In `lib/integrations/sanity/queries.ts`:

```ts
export const BLOG_QUERY = defineQuery(`
  *[_type == "blog" && slug.current == $slug][0] {
    _id,
    title,
    slug,
    excerpt,
    author,
    publishedAt,
    ${richTextWithLinks},
    tags,
    metadata,
    _updatedAt
  }
`;
```

Rules:
- Always include `_id`, `title`, `slug`, `_updatedAt`
- Use the existing `richTextWithLinks` fragment for any `content` field with Portable Text — it resolves internal links within rich text markup
- Use `$slug` parameter — `SanityFetch` passes it automatically
- Include all fields you want to render in the markdown output

### 3. Create the route handler

Create `app/api/blog/[slug]/route.ts`:

```ts
import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { portableTextToMarkdown } from "@/lib/utils/portable-text-to-markdown";
import { isSanityConfigured } from "@/lib/integrations/check-integration";
import { BLOG_QUERY } from "@/lib/integrations/sanity/queries";
import { SanityFetch } from "@/lib/integrations/sanity/live";

export async function GET(
  _request: Request,
  props: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> },
) {
  const { slug: rawSlug } = await props.params;

  if (!rawSlug.endsWith(".md")) {
    return new NextResponse(null, { status: 404 });
  }

  const slug = rawSlug.slice(0, -3);
  const baseUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL || "http://localhost:3000";

  if (!isSanityConfigured()) {
    return new NextResponse("# 404 Not Found\n\nCMS not configured.", {
      status: 404,
      headers: { "Content-Type": "text/markdown; charset=utf-8" },
    });
  }

  try {
    const blog = await SanityFetch(slug, BLOG_QUERY, "Blog Post");

    // SanityFetch returns NextResponse on error — pass it through
    if (blog instanceof NextResponse) return blog;

    const parts: (string | null)[] = [
      `# ${blog.title}`,
      "",
      blog.excerpt ? `> ${blog.excerpt}` : null,
      "",
      blog.author ? `**Author:** ${blog.author}` : null,
      blog.publishedAt
        ? `**Published:** ${new Date(blog.publishedAt).toLocaleDateString()}`
        : null,
      blog._updatedAt
        ? `**Updated:** ${new Date(blog._updatedAt).toLocaleDateString()}`
        : null,
      blog.tags?.length ? `**Tags:** ${blog.tags.join(", ")}` : null,
      "",
      "---",
      "",
      portableTextToMarkdown(blog.content),
      "",
      "---",
      "",
      `[View all content](${baseUrl}/sitemap.md)`,
    ];

    const markdown = parts.filter((part) => part !== null).join("\n");

    return new NextResponse(markdown, {
      headers: {
        "Content-Type": "text/markdown; charset=utf-8",
        Vary: "Accept",
        "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
      },
    });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Error fetching blog markdown:", error);
    return new NextResponse("# 500 Error\n\nFailed to fetch blog post.", {
      status: 500,
      headers: { "Content-Type": "text/markdown; charset=utf-8" },
    });
  }
}
```

**Route handler rules:**

- Always validate `rawSlug.endsWith(".md")` first — return 404 if missing
- Strip `.md` with `rawSlug.slice(0, -3)` to get the actual slug
- Check `isSanityConfigured()` before querying
- Use `SanityFetch(slug, query, label)` — it handles 404/500/503 errors
- Check `if (result instanceof NextResponse) return result` to propagate error responses
- Use `portableTextToMarkdown()` for any Portable Text / rich text field
- Include a link to `/sitemap.md` at the bottom
- Set `Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8` on all responses
- Map **every schema field** to markdown — dates formatted, arrays joined, booleans as text

### 4. Update the link resolver

In `lib/integrations/sanity/utils/link.ts`, add the new type to `CONTENT_TYPE_TO_PATH`:

```ts
export const CONTENT_TYPE_TO_PATH: Record<string, string> = {
  article: "/blog",
  blog: "/blog",       // add this
};
```

This ensures `resolveMarkdownUrl` generates correct `.md` links when other content types reference blog posts via internal links.

### 5. Update the sitemap

In `app/sitemap.md/route.ts`, add a query and section for the new type:

```ts
// In the fetch block, add:
const [articles, blogs] = await Promise.all([
  // ... existing queries ...
  client.fetch<SanityDoc[]>(
    groq`*[_type == "blog" && defined(slug.current)] | order(publishedAt desc) {
      title,
      slug,
      _updatedAt
    }`,
  ),
]);

// After the existing sections, add:
if (blogs.length > 0) {
  parts.push("## Blog Posts", "");
  for (const blog of blogs) {
    parts.push(
      `- [${blog.title}](${baseUrl}/blog/${blog.slug.current}.md)`,
    );
  }
  parts.push("");
}
```

## Field to Markdown Mapping

| Schema Field Type | Markdown Output |
|---|---|
| `string` (title) | `# ${value}` |
| `text` (excerpt) | `> ${value}` |
| `string` (author) | `**Author:** ${value}` |
| `datetime` | `**Published:** ${new Date(value).toLocaleDateString()}` |
| `array of strings` (tags) | `**Tags:** ${value.join(", ")}` |
| `array of blocks` (content) | `portableTextToMarkdown(value)` |
| `image` | Handled automatically inside `portableTextToMarkdown` |
| `reference` (internal link) | `[${text}](resolveMarkdownUrl(ref, baseUrl))` |
| `url` (external link) | `[${text}](${url})` |
| `slug` | Not rendered directly — used for routing |
| `object` (metadata) | Not rendered — used for SEO only |

## Markdown Structure Convention

Every route handler should produce this structure:

```markdown
# Title

**Field:** value
**Field:** value

---

[main content from Portable Text]

---

[View all content](baseUrl/sitemap.md)
```

- Title as `h1`
- Metadata fields as bold key-value pairs
- Horizontal rules to separate metadata from content
- Footer link back to sitemap for navigation

## SanityFetch Helper

The `SanityFetch` function in `lib/integrations/sanity/live/index.tsx` wraps `sanityFetch` with standardized markdown error handling:

```ts
const result = await SanityFetch(slug, yourQuery, "Label");
if (result instanceof NextResponse) return result; // Error response (404, 500, 503)
// result is now your data
```

It returns:
- **503** — CMS client unavailable
- **404** — Document not found (null data)
- **500** — Query execution error
- **Data** — The fetched document on success

When adding a new content type, verify all of these:

- [ ] Route handler at `app/api/{type}/[slug]/route.ts` with `.md` extension validation
- [ ] Route added to `markdown-proxy.config.ts` (`mdExtensionRoutes`)
- [ ] `CONTENT_TYPE_TO_PATH` updated in `utils/link.ts`
- [ ] Sitemap section added in `app/sitemap.md/route.ts`
- [ ] Test: `curl http://localhost:3000/{type}/{slug}.md` returns markdown
- [ ] Test: `curl http://localhost:3000/sitemap.md` lists the new content
